category_title: High school students with learning disabilities and ADHD who struggle to break down multi-step algebraic tasks
minimal_context: The student is transitioning from using Algebra Lab Gear to using abstract symbols with the Box Method during a one-on-one instructional session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: For this next problem, let's transition away from the Algebra Lab Gear and try using abstract symbols only with the Box Method.

STUDENT: I'm not good at that. I don't know if I am doing this right.

TUTOR: Just write down your steps in the boxes and see what you get.

STUDENT: Okay, I filled in the abstract symbols, but I know I messed up the solution.

TUTOR: Look at the work you just did. What do you think?

STUDENT: This is all wrong (handing me her paper). You aren't even helping me!

options.A: Terminate the demands and remove the Box Method materials from the student for 10 seconds during the session.
options.B: Ask the student to describe the form of the abstract symbols she just wrote down in the boxes.
options.C: Encourage the student to rely on the tools (Algebra Lab Gear and Box Method) rather than the tutor for verification.
options.D: Provide the student with a warning about the transition to the next instructional activity during the session.
